MedCat.evidence_source: In Study 2, 185 Chinese children in Beijing were followed for 8 months. We found that a pessimistic explanatory style was associated with higher concurrent levels of depressive symptoms and higher levels at subsequent tests as well. ... At the post-test and the 3- and 6-month follow-ups, children who participated in the intervention program showed significantly fewer depressive symptoms. A more optimistic explanatory style mediated the prevention of depressive symptoms.
